<a name="Axes"></a>

## Axes

A setting of the active app's plot view, 0 on a reset calculator.

| | |
|---|---|
| Syntax | `Axes` → real |
| Syntax | `Axes:=value` |
| Group | common-plot-view |
| Runs on the PC | no |

### Examples

| Call | Result | Known from |
|---|---|---|
| `EXPR("Axes")` | `0` | [emulator](results.tsv) |
| `LOCAL o; o := EXPR("Axes"); EXPR("Axes:=" + STRING(o)); RETURN EXPR("Axes");` | `0` | [emulator](results.tsv) |

### Behaviour

**What it holds is read from its name** (unverified): HP's list gives the name, the
group, and nothing more. Whether 0 means on or off is not known.

**Measured with the Function app active** (emulator), the state every batch starts
in, [apps.reset-leaves-function-active](../topics/apps.md#apps.reset-leaves-function-active). Whether another
app holds a different value was not tried (unverified).

**A program can assign it** (emulator): given its own value back, it was
accepted and read back the same. Another value was not tried.

The interpreter does not implement it, so `hpprime run` cannot check a program
that uses it (unverified).

[Cursor](common-plot-view/Cursor.md) · [GridDots](common-plot-view/GridDots.md) · [GridLines](common-plot-view/GridLines.md) · [Labels](common-plot-view/Labels.md)

<a name="ImageOpacity"></a>

## ImageOpacity

How opaque the picture behind the active app's plot is, 75 on a reset calculator.

| | |
|---|---|
| Syntax | `ImageOpacity` → real |
| Syntax | `ImageOpacity:=value` |
| Group | common-plot-view |
| Runs on the PC | no |

### Examples

| Call | Result | Known from |
|---|---|---|
| `EXPR("ImageOpacity")` | `75` | [emulator](results.tsv) |
| `LOCAL o, r; o := EXPR("ImageOpacity"); IFERR EXPR("ImageOpacity:=50"); r := EXPR("ImageOpacity"); THEN r := "refused"; END; EXPR("ImageOpacity:=" + STRING(o)); RETURN r;` | `50` | [emulator](results.tsv) |

### Behaviour

**What it holds is read from its name** (unverified): HP's list gives the name, the
group, and nothing more.

**Measured with the Function app active** (emulator), the state every batch starts
in, [apps.reset-leaves-function-active](../topics/apps.md#apps.reset-leaves-function-active). Whether another
app holds a different value was not tried (unverified).

**A program can set it** (emulator): set to 50, it read back 50. Each row that sets it reads the first value, sets another, reads again and
puts the first one back, so no later row of the batch saw the change.

That 75 is a percentage is read from the value (unverified).

The interpreter does not implement it, so `hpprime run` cannot check a program
that uses it (unverified).

[ImageName](common-plot-view/ImageName.md) · [ImageDisplay](common-plot-view/ImageDisplay.md)

<a name="Nmax"></a>

## Nmax

The last index plotted of a plot, refused while the Function app is active.

| | |
|---|---|
| Syntax | `Nmax` → real |
| Group | common-plot-view |
| Runs on the PC | no |

### Examples

| Call | Result | Known from |
|---|---|---|
| `EXPR("Nmax")` | *error* | [emulator](results.tsv) |
| `LOCAL o, r; o := EXPR("Nmax"); IFERR EXPR("Nmax:=20"); r := EXPR("Nmax"); THEN r := "refused"; END; EXPR("Nmax:=" + STRING(o)); RETURN r;` | *error* | [emulator](results.tsv) |

### Behaviour

**Read and set alike, it was refused with the Function app active**
(emulator), where the window's `Xmin` and `Ymax` answered. So, as with some
app functions and variables, it needs its own app active, [apps.function-needs-active-app](../topics/apps.md#apps.function-needs-active-app).

**Which app that is, the Sequence app, is read from its name** (unverified): HP's
list files it with the plot settings every app shares, and gives nothing
more. With that app active it was not tried, so no value and no form that
sets it is given here.

The interpreter does not implement it, so `hpprime run` cannot check a program
that uses it (unverified).

### Related

[Xmin](common-plot-view/Xmin.md) · [apps.function-needs-active-app](../topics/apps.md#apps.function-needs-active-app)

### Behaviour

**Read and set alike, it was refused with the Function app active**

**Which app that is, the Parametric app, is read from its name** (unverified): HP's

sets it is given here.

The interpreter does not implement it, so `hpprime run` cannot check a program
that uses it (unverified).

<a name="Xmax"></a>

## Xmax

The right edge of the active app's plot window, 15.9 on a reset calculator.

| | |
|---|---|
| Syntax | `Xmax` → real |
| Syntax | `Xmax:=value` |
| Group | common-plot-view |
| Runs on the PC | no |

### Examples

| Call | Result | Known from |
|---|---|---|
| `EXPR("Xmax")` | `15.9` | [emulator](results.tsv) |
| `LOCAL o, r; o := EXPR("Xmax"); IFERR EXPR("Xmax:=5"); r := EXPR("Xmax"); THEN r := "refused"; END; EXPR("Xmax:=" + STRING(o)); RETURN r;` | `5` | [emulator](results.tsv) |

### Behaviour

**Measured with the Function app active** (emulator), the state every batch starts
in, [apps.reset-leaves-function-active](../topics/apps.md#apps.reset-leaves-function-active). Whether another
app holds a different value was not tried (unverified).

**A program can set it** (emulator): set to 5, it read back 5. Each row that sets it reads the first value, sets another, reads again and
puts the first one back, so no later row of the batch saw the change.

**The drawing commands follow it** (emulator), because the forms without
`_P` count the plot window's own units, [interface.draw-units](../topics/interface.md#interface.draw-units). With the window a reset
calculator has, `C→PX(0,0)` answers `{160,109}`; with `Xmin` at 0 it answered
`{1,109}`, and with `Ymax` at 0, `{160,0}`: the point moved to the window's
edge. So a program drawing in units draws somewhere else once anything has
changed the window.

The interpreter does not implement it, so `hpprime run` cannot check a program
that uses it (unverified).

### Related

[Xmin](common-plot-view/Xmin.md) · [Ymax](common-plot-view/Ymax.md) · [interface.draw-units](../topics/interface.md#interface.draw-units)
